Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. 3. Voriconazole also increases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Esomeprazole increases the levels of bismuth subsalicylate by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 10. Blessed thistle decreases the effects of esomeprazole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This is a theoretical interaction, and the clinical significance is unknown. 11. Esomeprazole increases the levels or effects of bosentan by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 12. Esomeprazole decreases the effects of capecitabine through an unknown mechanism. Retrospective data suggest that elevated gastric pH caused by proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) may impair capecitabine tablet dissolution and/or reduce absorption. However, a randomized crossover study found that esomeprazole did not affect capecitabine systemic exposure. 13.
